title: UED Reconstruction Programme — Paper 14: Cross-Technology and Cross-Observation Unification Audit
summary: Paper 14 of the UED Reconstruction Programme performs the first explicit cross-technology and cross-observation unification audit across the reconstructed regimes developed in Papers 1–13. The paper distinguishes conceptual breadth from physical unification. Repeated terminology is not treated as evidence of a unified mechanism. Genuine unification is required to preserve operational variable identity, dimensional continuity, shared parameters, independent calibration, and cross-domain predictive closure. A domain-indexed forward-model architecture is introduced in which measured outputs are represented through shared and domain-specific parameters. The audit defines a joint residual statistic, a standardized shared-parameter closure measure, leave-one-domain-out prediction, a descriptive patch-burden ratio, and five maturity levels ranging from interpretive correspondence to cross-domain prediction. The strongest present bridges are identified as energy accounting across mechanical, electrical, and thermal systems; Planck’s constant across optical detection, atomic spectroscopy, and clocks; statistical use of Boltzmann’s constant across thermal regimes; and the common gravitational organization potential linking mechanical, clock, and optical response channels. Important missing bridges remain explicit. Generic SVE ripple variables lack absolute metrological calibration; the optical ripple state has not been derived from electrical and magnetic variables; ATT has a rigorous first-passage definition but no universal cross-technology response coefficient; nonlinear strong-gravity closure remains unknown; and dynamic-path redshift has not yet acquired an independently predicted nonzero law. The paper also imposes external correspondence constraints from equivalence-principle tests, precision optical clocks, compact-object imaging, gravitational-wave observations, and cosmological datasets. The strict Still-Universe branch is required to survive joint cosmological data closure without inserting unconstrained functions or hidden geometric-expansion terms. Paper 14 concludes that the UED Reconstruction Programme has achieved a coherent variable grammar and several genuine operational cross-domain bridges, but has not yet achieved a parameter-complete unified physical theory. It therefore converts unification from a declaration into a reproducible calibration, prediction, and falsification programme.

title: The Impact of Supply Chain Resilience on Corporate Green Innovation: Evidence from Chinese A-Share Listed Firms
summary: Against a backdrop of frequent external shocks and an accelerating green transition, this study examines whether supply chain resilience improves firms' current green innovation. Using 2004-2024 panel data for Chinese A-share listed firms, we construct supply chain resilience as the sum of entropy-weighted resistance and recovery indices. Two-way fixed-effects estimates show that all three measures significantly increase green patent applications. The findings remain robust to leave-one-out industry-year instrumental-variable estimation, alternative samples, expanded controls, and an alternative resilience measure. Mechanism tests indicate that resilience supports green R&D by easing financing constraints and reducing agency costs, while corporate reputation and ownership concentration improve the conversion of resilience resources into innovation. The effect differs across listing boards, ownership types, and factor intensities: it is stronger for non-GEM, state-owned, and labor-intensive firms, but becomes negative for GEM firms. Supply chain resilience is therefore not merely an operational safeguard; it is also an organizational capability that sustains green innovation. The evidence provides a firm-level basis for jointly advancing supply chain security and green transformation.

title: Corporate disclosures of carbon-reduction actions and firm value: the moderating role of digital transformation
summary: Purpose This study examines whether corporate disclosures of carbon-reduction actions are associated with firm value under China's “dual-carbon” strategy. It further compares the valuation relevance of internally oriented operational disclosures and value-chain-oriented disclosures and investigates the moderating role of digital transformation. Design/methodology/approach Using Chinese A-share listed firms from 2013 to 2023, this study develops a machine-learning-assisted textual measurement approach to identify disclosures of carbon-reduction actions from annual reports, environmental, social and governance (ESG) reports and sustainability reports. Fixed-effects regressions are employed to test valuation effects, with additional analyses on moderating effects, mediating mechanisms and firm heterogeneity. Findings Corporate disclosures of carbon-reduction actions are positively associated with firm value. This association is stronger for internally oriented operational disclosures than for value-chain-oriented disclosures. Digital transformation negatively moderates both associations. Channel tests provide evidence consistent with three mechanisms: improved trade credit, stronger media reputation and enhanced green innovation. Practical implications Firms should improve differentiated carbon disclosure across emission scopes and coordinate resource allocation across digital and green initiatives. Policymakers should strengthen disclosure standards and provide targeted support for small and medium-sized firms to enhance collaborative carbon reduction and green innovation. Originality/value This study introduces an emission-scope-informed perspective into research on the market valuation of carbon-reduction disclosures and develops a machine-learning-assisted approach for identifying firm-level disclosures of carbon-reduction actions.

title: Seeing Is More than Believing: ESG Performance Aspiration Gap and Institutional Investors’ Site Visits
summary: ESG has profoundly influenced asset pricing and resource allocation in capital markets. However, existing research largely focuses on the economic consequences of absolute ESG levels, with limited attention paid to how the gap between corporate ESG performance and aspiration levels—the ESG performance aspiration gap—is related to the behavior of information intermediaries in the capital market. Using a sample of A-share non-financial listed companies on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange from 2013 to 2024, this paper empirically examines the relation between the ESG performance aspiration gap and institutional investors’ site visits and its potential underlying channel. The findings are as follows. First, the ESG performance aspiration gap is positively correlated with institutional investors’ site visits. This conclusion remains robust after a series of robustness tests. Second, the mechanism analysis is consistent with information asymmetry serving as a potential channel linking the ESG performance aspiration gap and institutional investors’ site visits. Third, the moderating effect analysis shows that both marketization level and analyst coverage negatively moderate the positive relation between the ESG performance aspiration gap and institutional investors’ site visits. This paper extends the research boundaries of the economic consequences of ESG and institutional investors’ information search behavior, providing a new theoretical explanation for how the capital market responds to the dynamic changes in corporate ESG performance. It also offers policy implications for improving the ESG information disclosure system and enhancing the information efficiency of the capital market.

title: Corporate governance, corporate social responsibility, political connections, and tax avoidance in a developing country: A systematic literature review of Indonesian evidence
summary: Tax avoidance is a central corporate-governance and fiscal issue in developing countries, where tax revenues are important but enforcement and governance quality remain heterogeneous. This systematic literature review synthesizes Indonesian corporate evidence on Good Corporate Governance (GCG), Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR), political connections, and tax avoidance. Following the PRISMA 2020 logic, the review documented 14 records identified through Google Scholar and SINTA searches conducted with Publish or Perish, supplemented by Scopus and Web of Science verification. After screening and eligibility assessment, 11 primary empirical studies were retained and three records were excluded as out-of-scope or secondary/contextual literature. The synthesis indicates that political connections are the most consistently reported positive correlate of tax avoidance, although the relationship is not universal. Conventional GCG proxies do not consistently reduce tax avoidance in isolation, while CSR produces ambivalent results that are consistent with both an ethical-constraint mechanism and a legitimacy-shield mechanism. Firmansyah et al. (2022) provides particularly strong evidence: political connections and investment opportunity sets increase tax avoidance, whereas CSR disclosure weakens those positive effects. Measurement heterogeneity, especially differences among ETR, CETR, BTD, and related proxies, contributes to divergent findings. The review concludes with implications for tax-risk profiling, governance evaluation, and future causal research.

title: Unleashing Green Vitality: The Impact of the Digital Economy on Green Innovation in Resource-Based Cities
summary: Resource-based cities are often characterized by concentrated industrial structures, energy-intensive production, and substantial pressure for technological transformation. Whether digitalization can strengthen green technological innovation in these cities remains an important empirical question. Using a balanced panel of 114 Chinese resource-based cities over the period 2011–2019, this study evaluates the implications of digital economy development for green technological innovation. The empirical strategy combines two-way fixed-effects estimation with alternative measurements, dynamic panel estimation, instrumental-variable identification, and a quasi-natural experiment based on the “Broadband China” policy. The estimates consistently indicate that digital development increases green patenting in resource-based cities. Further evidence is consistent with a potential financial-development channel whereby digitalization may relax financing constraints and improve the allocation of financial resources toward innovation-oriented activities. The estimated impact is also amplified when environmental issues receive greater attention from local governments and the public. Nonlinear estimation identifies two critical values for both digital development and marketization, with the marginal innovation return to digitalization rising after each threshold is crossed. Taken together, the results show that digitalization can facilitate the technological transformation of resource-dependent economies, but its effectiveness is contingent on complementary financial capacity, environmental governance, and market institutions.

title: ESG Disclosure and Real Earnings Management in High-Polluting Industries: The Moderating Role of Audit Quality
summary: The current research looks at how Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) disclosure affects real earnings management (REM) and how audit quality (AQ) moderates this relationship. The study sample consists of 292 firm-year observations for the period 2022–2025 from 73 non-financial firms in highly polluting industries listed on the Saudi Stock Exchange (Tadawul). Panel regression analyses and an alternative estimator (pooled OLS with robust standard errors) are used to assess the robustness of the results. The findings show that REM is negatively associated with ESG disclosure, suggesting that firms with higher ESG disclosure have lower REM. However, the moderating hypothesis (H2) is not supported by the present evidence since the interaction between ESG disclosure and AQ is not statistically significant in any of the specifications estimated. The absence of a significant interaction is viewed as a lack of statistically measurable moderation as specified here. Based on an integrated Agency and Stakeholder Theory framework, the study considers ESG disclosure and AQ as mechanisms that increase the expected penalty for managerial opportunism and the expected probability of detection, respectively, and therefore suggests a positive relationship between the two; hence, the two mechanisms were expected to act as complements, not substitutes. The evidence confirms the first mechanism, but there is no evidence for the conjunction, indicating that the complementarity is conditional and is not yet available in the Saudi environment because of the lack of an assurance mandate for non-financial information. The study provides new insights from an emerging market and establishes the limitations of ESG disclosure and audit quality in limiting REM together.

title: Exploring the Potential of Green Finance: a Narrative Literature Review
summary: Objective: Investigate the potential of green finance in order to explore its impact on environmental sustainability and the financial performance of companies. Theoretical Framework: The fundamental concepts underpinning the research are presented, with a focus on green finance, sustainable investments, green bonds, and ESG criteria. This provides a solid basis for understanding the research context. Method: The research was conducted through a narrative review of the literature with a bibliographic and qualitative nature, involving scientific references in the Google Scholar and CAPES periodical databases. A total of 45 relevant publications were selected from the database using a combination of keywords to present the results of this study. Results and Discussion: The findings indicate that green finance implementations exert a favorable influence on environmental sustainability, underscoring the efficacy of green financial instruments in promoting sustainable projects and, consequently, fostering renewable energy production and enhancing energy efficiency. The analysis further indicates a growing body of literature on green finance, underscoring the importance of sustainable finance in the current global context. Research Implications: The practical and theoretical implications of this research reflect on how green finance can be integrated into business strategies and influence practices in the field of financial management, contributing to sustainability. Originality/Value: It contributes to the literature by offering a comprehensive review of green finance, highlighting its relevance in a growing context of environmental concern and the need for responsible financial practices.

title: Audit committee characteristics, corporate environmental sustainability and earnings management strategy: An empirical study of Saudi Arabia-listed companies
summary: This study aimed to explore the link between audit committee (AC) characteristics and earnings management (EM) in Saudi listed companies and assess the effect of corporate environmental sustainability (assessed using corporate social responsibility (CSR)-related measures) on the relationship between the two. The study draws data from a panel of 131 firms listed on the Saudi Exchange from 2015 to 2021, comprising 917 firm-year observations. In the baseline model, the results show that meetings between the AC and the board are negatively related to EM. In the baseline analysis, however, there were no significant effects on the size and independence of the AC. Furthermore, the moderating analysis shows that the interaction between CSR and AC size is positive and statistically significant, while the interaction between CSR and AC independence is positive and marginally significant. However, the relationship between CSR and AC meetings is not statistically significant. The results indicate that the effect of AC characteristics on EM is dependent on firms’ CSR involvement. The results from the robustness tests conducted using feasible generalized least squares (FGLS) and two-stage least squares (2SLS) estimations also give results similar to those of the baseline model, which ensures the reliability and stability of the main findings.

title: Developing environmental performance in the Bangladesh banking sector: role of fintech, climate finance and environmental awareness
summary: This study aims to investigate the relationship between climate banking and the environmental performance of banks in Bangladesh, focusing on climate finance, environmental awareness, and the role of FinTech. The study used the partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) technique to analyse data from 312 bank practitioners. The results revealed that climate banking practices (CBP) are positively associated with climate finance (CF), environmental awareness (EA), and FinTech adoption (FA). CF and FA are positively related to the bank’s environmental performance (BEP), while EA determines both direct and indirect associations with BEP. FA and CF play a mediating role in the relationship between CBP and BEP. This research contributes to the first empirical understanding of how digital transformation and climate-aligned financing mechanisms can promptly promote sustainability in the Global South banking sector context. This builds the groundwork for understanding how increased climate change resilience can contribute to the sustainability and global competitiveness of banks in emerging economies. This also aids policymakers and banks in developing convergence strategies with global frameworks for sustainable development.

title: Financial and institutional pathways through which green finance and sustainable investment support the transition toward low-carbon economies
summary: This paper examines the relationship between green finance, sustainable investment and the transition toward low-carbon economies by reviewing the main theoretical and empirical contributions developed in recent literature. The analysis focuses on three complementary dimensions: the institutional and financial foundations of green finance, the integration of sustainability and climate risk into investment and asset-pricing decisions, and the capacity of sustainable finance to generate measurable changes in production, technological adoption and economic decarbonization. The reviewed studies show that green bonds, green loans, ESG-oriented investment and climate-related financial policies can influence capital allocation, but their effectiveness depends strongly on credible certification, transparent information, appropriate risk-sharing mechanisms and supportive institutional frameworks. The literature also indicates that carbon exposure and climate risk are progressively incorporated into asset prices and portfolio decisions, while investor preferences increasingly affect demand for environmentally responsible securities. Beyond financial markets, the evidence suggests that green finance can support renewable-energy deployment, green technological investment, sustainable supply-chain practices and improvements in green total factor productivity. The overall conclusion is that sustainable finance contributes most effectively to low-carbon transition when financial development is translated into concrete technological, organizational and productive changes capable of reducing the environmental intensity of economic activity.

title: Smart supply chains: industry 4.0 and resilience in the UAE food and beverage sector
summary: Introduction The United Arab Emirates (UAE) food and beverage (F&B) sector is structurally import-dependent and critical to national industrial diversification, food security, and circular economy goals, making supply chain resilience a strategic priority. This study investigates how the adoption of Industry 4.0 technologies (Internet of Things, artificial intelligence, big data analytics, blockchain, cyber-physical systems, and cloud computing) enhances supply chain resilience. Drawing upon the Resource-Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, the Dynamic Resource-Based View, and Supply Chain Resilience Theory, the research posits that Industry 4.0 adoption impacts resilience directly and indirectly via supply chain and dynamic capabilities as mediators, with digital organizational culture acting as a moderator. Methods A quantitative, cross-sectional research design was utilized, gathering data via a structured survey administered to 395 senior supply chain and operations managers within UAE F&B manufacturing companies. The collected dataset was analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) via SmartPLS with 5,000 resamples to evaluate measurement validity, structural paths, and moderation effects. Results The structural equation modeling results support all six hypothesized paths. Industry 4.0 technology adoption exerts a significant positive effect on supply chain capabilities ( β = 0.849, P < 0.01$) and dynamic capabilities ( β = 0.869, P < 0.01$). Both supply chain capabilities ( β = 0.735, P < 0.01$) and dynamic capabilities ( β = 0.769, P < 0.01$) positively influence supply chain resilience. Furthermore, Industry 4.0 adoption has a direct positive impact on resilience ( β = 0.856, P < 0.01$), and digital organizational culture positively moderates the technology-resilience relationship ( β = 0.729, P < 0.01$). Discussion The findings demonstrate that modernizing F&B supply chains requires more than standalone technological investments; digital tools must be combined with internal capability building and a supportive digital organizational culture. For UAE producers, leveraging solutions like IoT traceability and AI forecasting—underpinned by a data-driven culture—strengthens overall network adaptability and recovery. These insights align with national strategic frameworks such as the UAE Circular Economy Policy 2021–2031 and Operation 300bn.

title: The ESG−audit nexus: unpacking the mediating role of CSR strategy and contextual moderators
summary: Purpose This research aims to investigate the impact of environmental, social and governance (ESG) scores on the likelihood of conducting sustainability audits. In this context, the mediating role of corporate social responsibility (CSR) strategy and the moderating roles of company size and systematic risk are considered. Design/methodology/approach This study used panel data from 168,198 firm-year observations. Findings A positive and significant relationship was found between the overall ESG score and the likelihood of conducting sustainability audits. Additionally, the mediating role of the CSR strategy was confirmed, indicating that formalized CSR commitments facilitate the translation of ESG performance into sustainability audits. Moreover, company size and systematic risk, as moderating variables, strengthened the aforementioned relationship. Originality/value This study integrates and extends institutional theory (focusing on external pressures for ESG) and strategic choice perspective (focusing on internal CSR strategy) to explain corporate behavior. This theoretical triangulation provides a more nuanced explanation than single-theory studies, revealing CSR strategy as the critical linchpin translating external ESG pressures into formalized audit and assurance practices.

title: Managerial climate change attention and supply chain innovation effect: evidence from China
summary: Abstract This study examines the impact of customers’ managerial climate change attention on suppliers’ green innovation. The findings indicate a positive relationship between customers’ managerial climate change attention and suppliers’ green innovation. This relationship is further reinforced when customers possess comparatively stronger bargaining power. Customers’ managerial climate change attention promotes suppliers’ green innovation by redirecting suppliers’ managerial attention toward climate issues and by inducing greater R&D investment in response to anticipated demand. Further, the attention paid to climate change-related opportunity and physical shock have superior supply chain spillover effects over the attention paid to regulatory shock. Customers’ managerial climate change attention has positive effects on both the application and grant of green patents. This paper suggests a new green innovation effect rooted in managerial climate change attention.

title: Analysis of Indonesia's Regulatory Readiness in Facing the Cross-Border Digital Economy
summary: The development of the cross-border digital economy has brought about significant changes in global economic activity, including in Indonesia. The digital transformation, marked by the increasing use of e-commerce, fintech, digital platforms, and international electronic transactions, demands regulatory readiness capable of effectively managing the dynamics of the digital economy. This study aims to nalyse Indonesia’s regulatory readiness to face the cross-border digital economy and identify various challenges in implementing existing policies. The research method used is a qualitative approach with analytical descriptive methods. Research data was obtained through a literature review by reviewing various laws and regulations, scientific journals, books, articles, and official documents related to the digital economy and cross-border regulations. The results show that Indonesia already has various important regulations to support digital economy management, such as the Personal Data Protection Law (PDP Law), regulations on Trading Through Electronic Systems (PMSE), fintech policies, and supervision of digital payment systems. These regulations demonstrate the government’s readiness to build a safe and competitive digital ecosystem. However, regulatory implementation still faces various challenges, including suboptimal inter-agency coordination, the high threat of cybercrime, complex supervision of cross-border digital transactions, and low public digital literacy. In addition, the rapid development of digital technology means that regulations often lag behind innovations developing in society and the global market.

summary: Introduction. The integration of ESG principles into business activities has become one of the key trends in the development of modern enterprises, driven by the growing expectations of consumers, investors, public authorities, and other stakeholders regarding environmental responsibility, social accountability, and sound corporate governance. Under these conditions, marketing distribution policy is no longer limited to organizing the physical movement of goods from producers to consumers. Instead, it is evolving into a strategic instrument for ensuring sustainable development, enhancing enterprise competitiveness, and creating long-term value for all market participants. Purpose. The purpose of this article is to investigate the theoretical foundations and practical aspects of integrating ESG principles into the development of a modern marketing distribution policy, to identify the key directions for their implementation in the management of distribution channels, logistics processes, and interactions among supply chain participants, and to develop a conceptual model of an ESG-oriented marketing distribution policy. Methods. The methodological framework of the study is based on the concepts of sustainable development, ESG management, marketing management, logistics, and supply chain management. The research employs systemic, process-oriented, comparative, and structural-logical approaches, as well as methods of analysis, synthesis, and generalization of scientific literature. The application of these methods made it possible to identify the interrelationships between environmental, social, and governance factors and the processes of developing marketing distribution policy, as well as to substantiate the mechanisms for integrating ESG criteria into the enterprise's managerial decision-making system. Results. The study identifies the main directions for integrating ESG principles into modern marketing distribution policy, including the implementation of environmentally sustainable logistics solutions, the development of socially responsible relationships with partners and intermediaries, the enhancement of corporate governance transparency, the application of digital technologies to improve supply chain traceability, and the assessment of ESG performance indicators. A conceptual model of an ESG-oriented marketing distribution policy is proposed, integrating environmental, social, and governance criteria into the strategic and operational management of distribution channels. It is substantiated that the implementation of the proposed approach contributes to improving distribution efficiency, strengthening partnerships, enhancing corporate reputation, and creating sustainable competitive advantages for enterprises. Conclusions. Modern marketing distribution policy should be developed based on the integration of ESG principles as a strategic foundation for ensuring enterprise sustainability. The incorporation of environmental, social, and governance criteria into distribution channel management enables the optimization of logistics processes, improves transparency in supply chain relationships, strengthens stakeholder trust, and enhances enterprise adaptability to contemporary market challenges. The proposed conceptual model of an ESG-oriented marketing distribution policy can serve as a methodological framework for improving enterprise distribution management systems and supporting the implementation of sustainable development strategies.

title: Methods for Supplier Default Risk Assessment in Supply Chains: A Review
summary: Supplier default risk represents a critical concern in supply chain management. This paper systematically reviews three quantitative approaches for supplier default risk assessment: weighted scoring, logistic regression, and Bayesian methods. The weighted scoring method constructs indicator systems with subjective or objective weights to rank suppliers by composite scores. Logistic regression models the log-odds of default as a linear function of supplier characteristics to estimate default probability. Bayesian methods, which are closely related to logistic regression, combine prior distributions with observed data to generate posterior probabilities, enabling dynamic updating and small-sample inference. Based on the comparative analysis, this paper proposes a multi-dimensional framework to guide method selection in procurement decisions. Research gaps and future directions are also identified, including dynamic updating mechanisms, integration of unstructured data, and the convergence of Bayesian methods with machine learning. Future research should explore real-time risk assessment and hybrid approaches that combine methods with machine learning to support more scientific supplier evaluation and enhanced supply chain resilience.

title: BYJU’S: An Edtech Startup Star Which Lost Its Lustre to Accounting Mistakes
summary: This case examined the accounting and financial-reporting issues that emerged during the rapid rise and subsequent decline of BYJU’S, once regarded as the leading company in India’s educational-technology sector. Founded by engineer and teacher Byju Raveendran, BYJU’S became India’s first edtech unicorn and was valued at US$22 billion in 2022. The company subsequently attracted scrutiny from investors, auditors, the media, and other stakeholders because of delays in completing its audited financial statements and concerns surrounding its revenue-recognition practices. Its valuation later declined substantially from its 2022 peak. title: Digital Transformation, Supply Chain Visibility, and Logistics Performance in Saudi Cement Logistics: A Descriptive-Analytical Literature Review
summary: In the cement industry, digital transformation is one of the key enablers for increased logistics efficiency, operability and supply chain integration. The key attributes of the cement supply chain in Saudi Arabia are that the demand centers are geographically spread out, the volume of transportation is high, logistics coordination is difficult among the fleets, the transportation delay is at the factory gate level and the need for reliable delivery performance. The descriptive-analytical approach of literature review has been adopted in this study to understand the role of digital transformation in supply chain visibility and logistics performance in Saudi cement logistics. The literature was examined and thematically analyzed in the context of three primary dimensions: digital logistics technologies, supply chain visibility and logistics performance outcomes. Technologies reviewed were GPS tracking, telematics, enterprise resource planning systems, Geographic Information Systems, artificial intelligence, digital dashboards and gate-system integration. The results show that digital transformation can impact logistics performance by increasing the connection of the real-time shipment monitoring, facilitating information sharing, assisting in route planning, coordinating dispatch, minimizing operational delays, and allowing data-driven decision-making. The analysis also reveals that the use of digital technologies for supply chain visibility is a central enabler that will drive delivery reliability, better use of fleet resources, responsiveness, cost control, and sustainability. Digital transformation applies particularly well to the Saudi context with long transport distances, concentrated industrial areas, increasing construction demand and the importance of logistics modernization and sustainability within the national agenda. The study found that digital transformation is not about digital tools alone, but is a systemic strategic and operational capability. The review makes a contribution by providing an industry-specific integration of the potential of digital technologies to improve visibility and logistics performance in Saudi cement value chains.

title: Managing the Bullwhip Effect in the Apparel Supply Chain through Omnichannel Strategies
summary: This technical report examines the bullwhip effect in apparel supply chains and explores how omnichannel retail strategies can mitigate demand distortions and improve supply chain responsiveness. The report explains how small fluctuations in consumer demand can amplify variability upstream among retailers, distributors, and manufacturers, leading to inefficiencies such as excess inventory, overproduction, higher costs, and reduced service performance. Drawing on established supply chain management literature, the report discusses the apparel industry's particular vulnerability to the bullwhip effect due to seasonality, fashion volatility, high SKU complexity, and rapidly changing consumer preferences. The report further analyzes the role of omnichannel strategies, including real-time inventory visibility, integrated demand forecasting, flexible fulfillment systems, responsive production models, and consumer behavior analytics, in reducing uncertainty and enhancing supply chain resilience. Designed for students, practitioners, and researchers, this publication provides an accessible overview of the relationship between omnichannel retailing and supply chain performance in the contemporary apparel industry.

title: Illusory Finance and Accounting Deception: Forensic Diagnostic Indices for Debt Bubbles and Earnings Management[cite: 1
summary: Abstract & Overview: This technical white paper represents the third installment in the foundational research series dedicated to institutional pathology, accounting manipulation, and operational immunity engineering (Beyond Management Series: Volume I). Moving beyond standard financial reporting, this paper addresses the systemic dangers of illusory finance, creative accounting, and speculative debt bubbles that drive distressed enterprises into "Ponzi finance" stages while masking structural decay behind clean book numbers. Core Diagnostic Contributions (Proposed Heuristic Indices): This paper formally introduces and mathematically models six original diagnostic indices and coefficients designed to expose accounting deception and monitor credit fragility: Earnings-Cash Flow Divergence Index (ECDI): Quantifies the relative gap between reported book net profits and actual cash collected from operations relative to total assets. Liquidity Exposure Coefficient (LEC): Measures the exponential divergence between profit growth and cash flow growth relative to total debt burdens. Bailout Capital Efficiency Index (BCEI): Evaluates the efficacy of bailout liquidity in actually restoring operational cash flow versus evaporating into legacy interest payments. Refinancing Bubble Index (RBI): Quantifies a firm's reliance on rolling over short-term managed debt relative to total operating revenues. Cumulative Collapse Coefficient (CCC): Tracks accelerating negative operational cash flow growth against new debt generation. Operating Core Depletion Ratio (OCDR): Measures the degree to which living operational assets are starved of capital to service past debt obligations. Methodological Status: In strict adherence to epistemic rigor, all indices are classified as Proposed Heuristic Indices intended for early-warning detection, operational diagnosis, and empirical testing in future longitudinal research.

title: The Role Of Blockchain Technology In Enhancing Financial Transparency And Auditing
summary: Financial scandals and the challenge of information asymmetries in corporate governance systems have revealed severe inadequacies in the existing systems of financial reporting and audits. Being inherently decentralized, immutable, and programmable, blockchain technology brings transformative capabilities to improve financial transparency and auditability in these systems. In this paper, we conduct a detailed study on how blockchain can be applied for financial transparency through a conceptual model that leverages three innovative features, such as triple entry accounting, automated compliance using smart contracts, and real time continuous auditing. We suggest a combination of permissioned blockchain architecture and cloud computing techniques to deal with scalability and regulatory issues that arise when applying blockchain in financial governance. Through our quantitative analysis, we show significant gains in the performance measures that include 88% decrease in audit delay time, 94% drop in data manipulation events, and 76% improvement in stakeholder trust index.

title: Do Transfer Pricing, CSR, Ownership Structure, and Earnings Management Affect Profitability Through Tax Avoidance? Evidence from Indonesian Manufacturing Firms
summary: Background/Motivation: Tax avoidance represents a persistent governance and fiscal challenge in emerging-market economies; however, its role as a mediating channel between firm-level strategic determinants and profitability remains underexplored in the Indonesian multinational context. Objective: This study examines whether transfer pricing, corporate social responsibility (CSR), managerial ownership, institutional ownership, and earnings management influence firm profitability through the intermediating mechanism of tax avoidance in Indonesian manufacturing multinational corporations (MNCs). Method: Using panel data from 31 IDX-listed MNCs over 2018–2023 (186 firm-year observations), we apply random effects panel regression and Sobel mediation tests, with robustness checks using Book-Tax Difference (BTD) as an alternative proxy, a lagged-variable specification, and an extended control variable set including financial leverage, capital intensity, sales growth, and year fixed effects. Endogeneity is assessed via the Durbin–Wu–Hausman test. Results: None of the five determinants significantly influences GAAP ETR, and tax avoidance does not significantly mediate any determinant–profitability relationship. Only institutional ownership exerts a significant direct effect on profitability (β = 0.002381, p < 0.05). Contribution: This is the first study to comprehensively test a five-determinant simultaneous mediation model in the Indonesian MNC context. The findings reveal that the mediation architecture commonly documented in developed-market contexts does not hold in Indonesian MNCs—attributable to institutional enforcement gaps, concentrated ownership structures, and the symbolic nature of CSR in emerging markets—with direct implications for Indonesian tax policy and corporate governance reform.

title: Using Probability Theory to Assess and Mitigate Risks in Global Supply Chains for Internationally Traded Goods and Services
summary: Global supply chains that support internationally traded goods and industrial services have become increasingly vulnerable to disruptions arising from geopolitical conflicts, economic uncertainty, climate-related disasters, cybersecurity threats, and transportation bottlenecks. These disruptions have exposed the limitations of conventional risk management approaches and created a growing need for quantitative methods capable of predicting uncertainty and supporting evidence-based decision making. Probability theory offers a rigorous analytical framework for assessing disruption likelihoods and improving supply chain resilience. This study investigates the application of probability theory in assessing and mitigating risks across global supply chains for internationally traded goods and services. A mixed-methods research design was employed, integrating Monte Carlo simulation, Bayesian networks, chi-square testing, Pearson correlation analysis, and multiple regression analysis to evaluate major supply chain risk factors and their operational impacts. The findings indicate that supply chain disruptions are not evenly distributed across regions, with North America and Europe experiencing the highest disruption frequencies, confirmed by the Chi-square test (χ² = 43.27, p < 0.01). Monte Carlo simulation showed that high-risk disruption events occur with probabilities ranging from 20% to 60%. Multiple regression analysis identified geopolitical risks (β = 1.50), economic downturns (β = 1.20), and supply chain congestion (β = 1.80) as the strongest predictors of supply chain disruptions (R² = 0.78, p < 0.001). Pearson correlation analysis further demonstrated a strong positive relationship between disruption frequency and economic losses (r = 0.85, p < 0.001). The study concludes that integrating probability-based analytical models significantly improves risk prediction, decision quality, and supply chain resilience. It recommends the adoption of real-time data analytics, artificial intelligence-driven forecasting, digital technologies, and collaborative risk-sharing mechanisms to strengthen the resilience of global supply chains for internationally traded goods and services.

title: Supply chain digitalization and innovation spillovers among peer enterprises
summary: Abstract With the rapid advancement of information technology, the digital transformation of supply chains has emerged as a pivotal pathway for enhancing enterprise innovation capabilities and market competitiveness. This study examines whether a city-level supply chain innovation and application pilot creates innovation spillovers among peer enterprises. Using Chinese A-share listed firms’ data and a difference-in-differences design, we find that policy exposure is associated with higher invention-patent innovation among industry peers and lower non-invention-patent innovation, a pattern that is also observed for regional peers. Mechanism analysis is consistent with three complementary channels: technology diffusion, enterprise digital transformation, and changes in supply chain concentration. The results suggest that digital supply chain reforms can redirect peer firms’ innovation portfolios toward more technology-intensive activities. Because non-invention patents may generate genuine economic value in some industries, we interpret their decline cautiously as a shift away from relatively strategic patenting rather than as evidence that all such patents are low quality. The study extends research on supply chain digitalization from focal-firm outcomes to industry and regional spillovers and offers implications for governments, industry platforms, and enterprise managers.

title: Tracking Transparency: Corporate Social Responsibility and Financial Performance Reporting in Canada’s Leading Food Chains
summary: The food industry in Canada faces many challenges, ranging from labor shortages to fluctuating prices and food safety, compounded by pressures related to climate change, market volatility, and growing sustainability requirements. In this constantly changing environment, companies in this industry must adapt their practices to ensure rigorous performance management and monitoring. This includes consideration of corporate social responsibility (CSR) regarding the economic, environmental, and social impacts of their actions. In that sense, this study examines how Canada's three largest food grocery chains - Sobeys, Metro, and Loblaw - measure and disclose their performance by analyzing the indicators presented in their various reports during the period of historic high inflation in food products for 2022 and 2023. Drawing on the neo-institutional and stakeholder theories, the study employs a qualitative content analysis of performance indicators disclosed in reports. The findings reveal both convergence and divergence in disclosure practices among the three chains. They use a variety of indicators covering several dimensions of performance and place particular emphasis on CSR issues, revealing a certain mimetic behavior in their performance measurement practices. One of the food chains differs from the other two in that it publishes no indicators on cybersecurity and food safety, and more indicators on sustainable sourcing. This study contributes to the literature on performance measurement and CSR disclosure in the food retail sector by providing insights into the indicators prioritized by the three major Canadian grocery chains and highlighting how they disclose performance to various stakeholders, including customers, during a period of economic uncertainty.

title: Tobacco Industry corporate social responsibility activities in Poland in the years 2019-2024
summary: INTRODUCTION: The tobacco industry frequently uses corporate social responsibility (CSR) activities to build relationships with stakeholders and maintain its legitimacy despite the health harms caused by its products. In Poland, where direct tobacco advertising is prohibited, CSR may serve as an indirect mechanism of industry influence. METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive review of publicly available information on CSR-related activities by the four largest tobacco companies in Poland (Philip Morris Polska, British American Tobacco Polska, Japan Tobacco International Polska, Imperial Tobacco Polska) from late 2019 through 2024. Sources included legal documents, government and local government websites, media reports, and the companies' social media, following a protocol aligned with the 6th recommendation of the Guidelines for Implementation of Article 5.3 of the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control (WHO FCTC). RESULTS: We identified four major categories of tobacco industry CSR activities: partnerships with educational institutions, cooperation with public institutions and government agencies, charitable initiatives, and engagement in policy and legislative processes. Across these categories, tobacco companies built relationships with public institutions and policymakers while presenting their activities as socially beneficial. Collectively, these activities extended beyond philanthropy, strengthening the industry's legitimacy despite restrictions on direct tobacco advertising. CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that tobacco industry CSR in Poland functions as a broader mechanism of influence rather than solely as a philanthropic activity. Strengthening the implementation of WHO FCTC Article 5.3, increasing awareness among public institutions, and ensuring greater transparency in interactions with the tobacco industry are essential to protect public health policymaking.

title: Linking digital transformation contextual conditions to quality performance through supply chain quality integration: a TOE and organisational information processing perspective
summary: Despite the prevalence of digital transformation (DT), the mechanisms through which manufacturing firms improve quality performance (QP) via supply chain quality integration (SCQI) remain underexplored. Rather than treating DT as a monolithic latent construct, we integrate the Technology-Organization-Environment (TOE) framework with organisational information processing theory (OIPT) to investigate how the technical, organisational, and environmental factors (TF, OF and EF) that underpin digitalisation relate to QP via internal and external quality integration (IQI and EQI). Surveying 414 Chinese manufacturers and using PLS-SEM, we find that all three conditions positively relate to both IQI and EQI, with TF-IQI and EF-EQI links being strongest. Both IQI and EQI drive QP, with EQI exhibiting a stronger coefficient. Mediation patterns differ: partial for TF, full for OF, and indirect via EQI for EF. This study clarifies the DT-measurement boundary, positions SCQI as a quality governance mechanism, and offers implications for digital-era supply chain quality management.

title: Do sustainability theories hold empirically? Evidence from a theory-driven systematic review of ESG and sustainability finance
summary: This study evaluates the empirical validity of seven influential sustainability theories, Stakeholder Theory, Legitimacy Theory, Institutional Theory, Agency Theory, the Resource-Based View, Dynamic Capabilities Theory, and Signaling Theory, within finance- and economics-oriented environmental, social, and governance (ESG) research. A theory-driven systematic review was conducted using Scopus and Web of Science and reported in accordance with PRISMA 2020. The final corpus comprised 67 peer-reviewed empirical studies. Each study was coded according to its focal theory, ESG operationalisation, financial outcome channel, methodological design, mechanism, and boundary conditions, and the evidence was classified as supported, partially supported, mixed, or contradicted using predefined adjudication rules. The findings reveal substantial variation in empirical support across theories. Agency Theory records the strongest within-corpus consistency, with all ten studies supporting its governance, monitoring, and incentive-alignment mechanisms. Legitimacy Theory and the Resource-Based View also receive strong support, particularly where substantive disclosure practices or embedded organisational resources are connected to financial outcomes. Stakeholder and Institutional theories show moderate and context-dependent support, whereas Signaling Theory and Dynamic Capabilities Theory produce weaker and more heterogeneous evidence. The explanatory strength of each theory varies across ESG measurement approaches, financial outcome channels, institutional settings, and methodological designs. Disclosure credibility is particularly important for signaling and legitimacy mechanisms, while capability-based explanations are stronger when ESG is measured through operational performance rather than disclosure alone. The study contributes a comparative theory-adjudication framework that moves beyond routine theory citation by identifying the mechanisms, outcome channels, and boundary conditions under which sustainability theories receive empirical support.

title: Green Logistics 5.0 and Sustainable Supply Chain Performance: Integrating Digital Innovation for Environmental Sustainability
summary: The increasing environmental impacts of logistics operations have intensified the need for sustainable logistics practices that balance economic growth with environmental responsibility. Green logistics has emerged as a strategic approach to reducing carbon emissions, minimizing waste, improving energy efficiency, and enhancing resource utilization across supply chains. Despite growing scholarly interest, the successful adoption of green logistics remains influenced by multiple technological, organizational, regulatory, and operational factors, particularly in emerging economies. This paper examines the key determinants of green logistics adoption and their implications for sustainable supply chain performance. Adopting a qualitative desktop research design based entirely on secondary literature synthesis, the study synthesizes evidence from peer-reviewed journal articles, policy documents, and reports published by reputable international organizations between 2020 and 2025. The review identifies environmental regulations and policies, technological advancements and innovations, supply chain collaboration and integration, energy efficiency in operations, waste minimization and sustainable packaging, resource availability and sustainable sourcing, organizational culture, and corporate social responsibility as critical drivers of green logistics implementation. The findings indicate that technological innovation and supportive regulatory frameworks significantly enhance the adoption of environmentally sustainable logistics practices, while collaboration among supply chain partners, organizational commitment, and responsible resource management further strengthen sustainability performance. The study concludes that an integrated approach combining technological advancement, effective governance, and stakeholder collaboration is essential for accelerating green logistics adoption. It recommends strengthening environmental policies, investing in digital logistics technologies, promoting sustainable business practices, and fostering cross-sector partnerships to support resilient and environmentally sustainable logistics systems that contribute to the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

title: The Price of Resilience: Input-Cost Shocks in European Supply Chains under EU Sanctions on Russia
summary: Version 1.04, 16.09.2026. Abstract Do broad-based sanctions cause physical supply chain breaks, or do they operate primarily as input-cost shocks? This paper uses the 2022 EU sanctions against Russia as a quasi-experimental shock to study the adjustment margins of European manufacturing. I map legal sanctions into trade data and propagate the shock downstream using the AI-generated Production Network (AIPNET), yielding a product-specific exposure measure capturing indirect reliance on sanctioned inputs. Using a dynamic difference-in-differences design for five major industrial economies (Germany, Denmark, Spain, France, Italy), I find that supply chains bent but did not break. While there is no robust evidence of a collapse in physical import volumes, CIF unit values—which measure landed procurement costs rather than quality-adjusted transaction prices—rose sharply for exposed goods. In the import-value-weighted benchmark specification, which targets aggregate expenditure incidence rather than the average product-line response, a 10 percentage point increase in exposure is associated with a 9.7% increase in the CIF import-cost margin. The price mechanism itself is identified separately through unit values. Applying the weighted incidence estimate to the 2021 import base yields a first-order border-expenditure accounting estimate of approximately 11.4 billion USD for the nine considered EU economies in 2022. I show that unlike the US trade war, where policy uncertainty caused extensive-margin adjustments, the hard constraint of the 2022 embargo generated an immediate resilience premium: in the shock period, exposed supply chains showed no robust collapse in physical import quantities while facing higher landed costs. The sanctions thus operated as a targeted input-cost shock at the border. The analysis does not identify how this additional import-side burden was ultimately divided between firm margins, downstream prices, quantities, and consumers. title: Board interlocks and earnings management: conditional effects across director type
summary: This study examines whether board interlocks are related to earnings management among KOSPI-listed firms in Korea from 2019 to 2024. Board interlocks may bring external information, experience, and reputational capital into the boardroom. The same ties, however, can weaken oversight when directors hold multiple appointments or when reporting practices travel through director networks. This study tests which interpretation better explains firms' financial reporting behavior. Earnings management is measured primarily by discretionary accruals from the Modified Jones model. Additional tests use the Kothari model, signed discretionary accruals and real earnings management. Board interlocks are measured at the total-board, inside-director, and outside-director levels, with further tests using alternative interlock definitions. The results show a positive relation between board interlocks and accrual-based earnings management. This relation remains evident across alternative interlock definitions and the Kothari-based measure. Signed accrual tests show that interlocks are related to larger discretionary accruals in both income-increasing and income-decreasing directions, rather than to one reporting direction alone. By contrast, the evidence for real earnings management is weaker, suggesting that the main results are concentrated in accrual-based reporting discretion. Director-type analyses indicate that inside- and outside-director interlocks capture different aspects of board networks, although neither type dominates across all specifications. Taken together, the evidence suggests that board interlocks in Korea are not merely advisory channels. They are also tied to weaker monitoring and the diffusion of reporting practices.

title: The scope and presentation of selected environmental disclosures under article 8 of the EU Taxonomy and ESRS Standards in the context of ESG reporting digitalisation
summary: Purpose: The article identifies and assesses diversity in the extent and presentation of selected environmental disclosures specified in the European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS) and the indicators required under Article 8 of the EU Taxonomy, as reported in sustainability reports. The assessment also covers the implications of such diversity for data comparability and digital processing. Methodology/approach: The first part of the article discusses the regulatory framework of the European Union (EU) Taxonomy and ESRS standards based on a review of the literature and legal regulations, as well as the role of digitalisation in sustainability reporting. The empirical study is based on a content analysis of the sustainability reporting of 66 companies from the EU operating in the construction and telecommunications sectors. The analysis focuses on disclosures related to energy intensity, greenhouse gas emission intensity, water intensity, and EU Taxonomy key performance indicators (turnover, CapEx, and OpEx). Findings: The results reveal significant differences in both the extent of disclosures and the way they are presented. These differences relate mainly to the units of measurement, numerical multipliers, and the level of detail provided. Environmental disclosures under the ESRS and indicators resulting from Article 8 of the EU Taxonomy were disclosed more frequently in the construction sector than in the telecommunications sector. Non-uniform presentation of data may limit their comparability and hinder automated processing in a digital environment. Originality/value: The article provides empirical evidence on the degree of diversity in how companies present environmental disclosures under the ESRS and Article 8 indicators. The originality of the study lies in combining the analysis of the scope and presentation of environmental disclosures with an assessment of the implications of such diversity for digitalisation and the automated processing of ESG data. The findings highlight the need for further standardisation of ESG data presentation and the development of digital reporting taxonomies that support the comparability and automated processing of ESG data.

title: Strategic agility and digital orientation as drivers of FinTech capability and organizational performance
summary: The emergence of Financial Technology (FinTech) has revolutionized the finance sector, emphasizing the necessity of an organization’s capabilities to enable digital transformation and innovation. A number of studies have identified the role of strategic agility, managerial digital orientation and innovation governance as critical components of an organization’s capacity to develop its ability to leverage FinTech. In this regard, this study assesses the relationship between strategic agility, managerial digital orientation and innovation governance with respect to the level of maturity of an organization’s FinTech capability. Furthermore, the study will investigate the impact of FinTech capability maturity on service innovation performance and organizational responsiveness among financial service organizations operating in Jordan. Based on dynamic capability theory and resource-based view (RBV), the study develops a theoretical model describing how various forms of managerial and strategic capabilities create value for organizations by enabling them to achieve higher levels of FinTech capability maturity. This study utilized a quantitative approach using partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS-SEM) via smart PLS 4. Data were collected using purposive sampling from 255 senior managers, specialists in digital transformation, innovation managers and professionals in FinTech working in Jordan banks and financial institutions and FinTech organizations. These respondents have direct knowledge of organizational initiatives related to digital transformation. Results of the measurement model showed high reliability, convergent validity and discriminant validity. Results of the structural model showed that all three independent variables (strategic agility, managerial digital orientation and innovation governance) had positive significant effects on FinTech capability maturity. Additionally, results indicated that FinTech capability maturity has significant positive relationships with both service innovation performance and organizational responsiveness. Results from this study add to the body of knowledge regarding FinTech and digital transformation by illustrating the significance of managerial capabilities to financial institutions to advance their organizational FinTech capability maturity in emerging markets such as Jordan. The results also offer practical applications for policymakers, regulatory bodies and financial institutions who are seeking to enhance their competitive position through innovations that provide greater adaptability and digital competences in increasingly changing economic environments.

title: Board diversity and financial reporting quality in Vietnamese banks
summary: Type of the article: Research ArticleAbstractGlobal financial crises over the past two decades have significantly increased academic attention to board diversity as an important aspect of corporate governance. This study examines the relationship between board diversity and financial reporting quality (FRQ) in listed Vietnamese commercial banks. The sample includes 27 Vietnamese banks observed over the period 2016–2024. Panel data are analyzed using a fixed effects model (FEM). Board diversity is examined along multiple dimensions, including gender diversity, educational level diversity, tenure diversity, age diversity, and a composite board diversity index that captures the overall level of board heterogeneity. FRQ is proxied by the absolute value of discretionary loan loss provisions (DLLP), where lower DLLP indicates higher reporting quality. The results show that greater overall board diversity is associated with higher FRQ. Among the individual diversity dimensions, only tenure diversity exhibits a statistically significant association with FRQ, whereas gender diversity, educational diversity, and age diversity do not show significant associations. Overall, the findings suggest that board tenure diversity and overall board heterogeneity are the primary drivers of the observed association between board diversity and FRQ in Vietnamese listed banks. The study is limited by the relatively small sample size, the focus on listed banks only, and the proxy-based measurement of FRQ.

title: The Consequences of ESG Rating Divergence on Corporate Transparency and Disclosure Practices
summary: This study aims to examine the consequences of ESG rating divergence on corporate transparency and disclosure practices using a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) approach. Twenty papers that satisfy the inclusion criteria are identified, screened, and subjected to content analysis as part of the study's investigation of international journal articles published between 2022 and 2026 and indexed in Scopus, Sinta and Garuda. The findings show that variations in rating agencies' evaluation techniques, indicators, weighting schemes, and data sources lead to ESG rating divergence, which can lead to information confusion and impact investor views in the capital markets. In order to lessen information asymmetry and boost stakeholder trust, the literature demonstrates that variations in ESG ratings motivate businesses to strengthen disclosure policies and increase openness. Reducing rating inconsistencies is found to be mostly dependent on improved ESG reporting quality, more access to sustainability data, and more robust governance structures. Additionally, corporations are driven to improve sustainability disclosure and openness by external forces like market surveillance, regulatory rules, and stakeholder expectations. Overall, the results indicate that ESG rating divergence offers corporate reporting both opportunities and challenges. While rating discrepancies may raise uncertainty, they also encourage businesses to strengthen transparency, improve disclosure quality, and increase accountability in sustainability reporting practices.

title: Cross-border supply chain finance research review: challenge response and model innovation
summary: Cross-border supply chain finance supports the financing of Small and Medium-sized Enterprises (SMEs) participating in the global division of labor by integrating logistics, information flow, and capital flow in cross-border trade. However, its development faces prominent challenges, such as cross-border information asymmetry, exchange rate and policy risks, difficulties in credit transmission, and complex regulatory coordination. In recent years, the application of fintech and blockchain technologies has driven the evolution of cross-border supply chain finance from a traditional bank-led single financing model toward a platform-based, digital, and ecosystem-oriented direction. This paper adopts a systematic literature review method to systematically examine the research progress of cross-border supply chain finance from three dimensions: challenges—responses—model innovation. At the challenge level, it focuses on barriers to cross-border credit transmission, exchange rate and compliance risks, and the difficulty of coordinating logistics, capital and information flows. At the response level, it summarizes strategies such as fintech empowerment, blockchain-based credit penetration, and multi-agent collaborative governance. At the model innovation level, it synthesizes emerging models, including cross-border e-commerce platform-led financing, blockchain-driven digital credit, and cross-border asset securitization. The study finds that existing research still has deficiencies in risk pricing, technology integration, and cross-regional regulatory coordination for cross-border supply chain finance. This paper proposes a three-dimensional analytical framework of "cross-border credit—technology empowerment—ecosystem synergy" and points out that future research can be deepened in directions such as digital credit infrastructure, smart contract risk control, cross-border regtech, and scenario expansion in emerging markets.

title: A Multi-Method Decision Framework for Assessing Barriers to Sustainable Perishable Agro-Product Supply Chains in Bangladesh
summary: The perishable agro-product supply chain in Bangladesh faces numerous barriers that contribute to food spoilage, economic losses, and reduced supply chain efficiency. Identifying and understanding the interrelationships among these barriers is essential for developing a resilient and sustainable supply chain. This study aims to identify, prioritize, and analyze the critical barriers affecting the perishable agro-product supply chain in Bangladesh. A three-phase methodology integrating the Delphi method, Best-Worst Method (BWM), and Interpretive Structural Modeling (ISM) was employed. Initially, barriers were identified through an extensive literature review and expert consultation. Subsequently, BWM was applied to rank the barriers based on their relative importance, while ISM was utilized to examine their hierarchical relationships and driving-dependence structure. The findings revealed 24 significant barriers affecting the supply chain. BWM results indicated that lack of government support for adopting green supply chain management (GSCM), product freshness depletion, informal payments to local influential groups and law-enforcement agencies, lack of support and guidance from regulatory authorities, and climate change are the most critical barriers. ISM analysis further demonstrated that lack of government support, lack of support and guidance from regulatory authorities, and climate change are the key driving barriers that significantly influence other supply chain obstacles. A nine-level hierarchical structure was developed to illustrate the interrelationships among the identified barriers. The proposed framework provides valuable insights for policymakers, practitioners, and supply chain managers to formulate effective risk mitigation strategies, enhance supply chain resilience, reduce food wastage, and promote sustainable agro-product supply chain management in Bangladesh.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Digital Transformation: How are Vietnamese Commercial Banks Creating Value?
summary: This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) and digital transformation (DT) are reshaping the operational performance of Vietnamese commercial banks, while clarifying the role of banking governance in translating technological capabilities into sustainable business value. The study adopts a qualitative approach, combining structured content analysis and thematic analysis of annual reports, financial statements, corporate governance reports, sustainability reports, and other official disclosures published by banks during the 2018–2025 period. The findings indicate that AI and digital transformation do not, in themselves, generate efficiency; rather, the value of technology emerges from the interplay of process digitalization, data exploitation, automation, service innovation, productivity enhancement, and risk management. Notably, digital maturity, data quality, human capital capabilities, and governance quality create substantial differences in banks’ ability to translate technology investments into operational outcomes. The study argues that the progress of digital transformation in banking should not be assessed by the number of technologies deployed, but by the capacity to convert technology into tangible gains in productivity, service quality, and substantive governance capabilities. On this basis, the study proposes policy and managerial implications for advancing banking digital transformation in a manner that is effective, secure, and sustainable.

title: The Inhibitory Effect of External Audit Quality on Corporate Information Disclosure Violations—An Empirical Test Based on A-Share Listed Companies
summary: Although information disclosure is crucial for capital market pricing efficiency and investor protection in recent years, the A-share market has still frequently exposed cases of financial fraud, false statements and other violations, and the market order and investors' trust have been damaged to varying degrees. Against this background, how to effectively curb corporate violations through external governance mechanisms has become an important issue. As a key external supervision force, independent audit plays an irreplaceable role in defense in preventing corporate compliance risks. For the 2015–2024 period, this paper examined A-share listed firms, measuring audit quality by the receipt of standard unqualified opinions and estimating the impact on disclosure violations through logit and probit regressions. This paper finds that the higher the audit quality, the lower the possibility of information disclosure violations. This is mainly because strict audit procedures can restrain opportunistic management behavior, thereby reducing the risk of violations. After controlling for fixed characteristics at the annual and industrial levels and re-estimating with a probit model, this result has not changed. This study enriches the relevant literature of external corporate governance, and provides empirical evidence for regulatory authorities to optimize differentiated inspection strategies and investors to assess the risk of corporate violations.

title: Audit Committee Attributes and Financial Reporting Quality of Selected Quoted Consumer Goods Firms in Nigeria
summary: The study investigated the effect of audit committee attributes on the quality of financial reporting among listed consumer goods firms in Nigeria. This was with a view to providing information on the relevance of audit committee attributes to the enhancement of financial reporting quality (FRQ) in Nigeria. The study adopted policeman theory to provide a richer basis to explain audit committee attributes influencing financial reporting disclosure. The study constructed an FRQ disclosure index with 93 as required by the Financial Reporting Disclosure standards issued by both international and local standard setters (IAS & IFRS). Content analysis technique was therefore used to measure FRQ as a dependent variable from the annual reports of the selected companies in line with the requirements of the index. Secondary data on audit committee attributes were also obtained from the company’s3 annual reports, the publication of the Nigeria Exchange Group (NXG) as well as the website of the companies. The study therefore used descriptive and panel data regression techniques to analyze data of 180 company observations from the sample from 2012 to 2023. The regression results exhibited that financial reporting quality is directly related to audit committee independence and size (β= 0.0796, p-value = 0.0169 and β= 0.0165, p-value = 0.0016) but inversely related to audit committee tenure (β= -0.0821, p-value = 0.0024) while audit committee meeting does not have a significant relationship with financial reporting quality (β= 0.0103, p-value = 0.6130). As regards the control variables, the results of the analysis demonstrate that firm age and financial leverage are positively related with financial reporting quality (β= 0.0060, p-value = 0.0000 and β= 0.0197, p-value = 0.0080) while firm size, return on assets, liquidity have insignificant relationship with financial reporting quality (β= 0.0450, p-value =0.5361, β= 0.0111, p-value = 0.0905; β= 0.0022, p value = 0.0811). The study concluded that audit committee attributes have the capacity to influence the financial reporting quality of listed consumer goods firms in Nigeria. The study therefore recommended that the corporate boards of listed consumer goods firms should encourage the appointment of non-executive directors into the audit committee to enhance the objectivity of the committee in taking decision in the best interests of all the stakeholders.

title: The Transformation of Corporate Social Responsibility PT Adaro Indonesia: From Aid to Economic Empowerment and Environmental Sustainability
summary: This study analyzes the transformation of PT Adaro Indonesia’s Corporate Social Responsibility initiatives in Jaro Village from material aid to economic empowerment and environmental sustainability as well as the factors driving and hindering this transformation. This research employs a qualitative method with a single-case study design, utilizing semi-structured interviews, participatory observation, and document analysis. The subjects involved include Corporate Social Responsibility managers, government representatives and village leaders, waste management groups, farmers and livestock breeders, as well as staff from the Environmental Agency. Data were analyzed using Yin’s case study design through pattern matching, explanation building, and time-series analysis. This study reveals that the transformation of Corporate Social Responsibility is reciprocal through collaboration between community initiatives and corporate support, shifting from the provision of resources to capacity building and the creation of sustainable value. Aid is transformed into capacity and productive assets through the maintenance, replication, and transfer of knowledge, linking the livestock, agriculture, and waste management sectors within a circular economy that utilizes local resources. Communities serve as problem identifiers and resource managers, while Corporate Social Responsibility supports local capacity building. Therefore, the success of Corporate Social Responsibility is influenced more by the ability to build collective capacity to maintain assets, create new value, and develop sustainable economic and environmental benefits, rather than solely by the amount of aid provided.
